exposure: uterine suture with aortic balloon and/or uterine artery embolization
outcome: early complications (late postpartum hemorrhage, fever, disseminated intravascular coagulation, organ injury)
late complications (menstrual changes, pelvic pain, urinary tract infections)
cohort: The study included 62 patients with placenta previa and placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) grades 2-3a who underwent cesarean section.
finding: Uterine suture with tourniquet binding during cesarean delivery for placenta previa with PAS grades 2-3a significantly reduced operative duration, postoperative hospitalization, hospitalization costs, transfusion costs, and early complication rates compared to uterine suture with aortic balloon and/or uterine artery embolization.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was measured as a baseline characteristic, but no specific range was provided.
gest_age: Gestational weeks at delivery were measured as a baseline characteristic, but no specific range was provided.
